recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中一顆吞噬性白血球的淡紫色細胞質內有多顆粗大、深藍黑色、大小不一的顆粒（吞噬的黑色素），明顯比正常嗜天青顆粒粗大深黑；此細胞核為腎形未分葉，形態偏向單核球或帶狀核細胞，而非典型分葉中性球。
features: Single leukocyte with a non-segmented, indented/reniform nucleus and moderately condensed chromatin
Multiple coarse, irregular blue-black cytoplasmic granules of variable size, clustered at the cell periphery (phagocytosed melanin pigment)
Granules are much coarser and darker than normal azurophilic or toxic granules
Background red cells with central pallor and drying/refractile artifact; no organisms
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a phagocytic leukocyte with an indented, non-segmented nucleus and pale, finely granular cytoplasm containing multiple coarse, irregular blue-black inclusions of variable size. The inclusions are distinctly larger and darker than toxic granulation or normal azurophilic granules. The nuclear shape of this particular cell is closer to a band neutrophil or monocyte than to a segmented neutrophil. Background red cells show refractile drying artifact without parasites. In a patient with metastatic melanoma, findings are consistent with phagocytosed melanin pigment in circulating phagocytes (melanin-laden leukocytes); a Fontana-Masson stain can confirm melanin.

ddx.vs: Toxic granules are fine, evenly distributed dark purple granules throughout the cytoplasm, not sparse coarse blue-black clumps.
Hemozoin is golden-brown to black refractile pigment accompanied by intraerythrocytic parasites, which are absent here.
Chediak-Higashi shows giant lysosomal granules in all granulocytes and Alder-Reilly shows diffuse dense granules in a congenital disorder, without an associated melanoma.
Organisms show regular shape, size and internal structure (cocci, yeasts with halos), unlike irregular amorphous pigment clumps.
